### The Mystery of the Unbending Beam
Imagine you are lost in a dense, dark forest. Suddenly, you see a sharp, straight beam of sunlight piercing through the leaves, illuminating a single spot on the ground like a spotlight. Have you ever wondered why this beam of light never curves around the trees? Why does it always cut perfectly straight through the dust?

### What do you think?
If you were to look at a glowing candle flame through a straight rubber tube, you would see the light easily. But if you bend the tube into a 'U' shape, can you still see the flame? What is stopping the light from traveling through the bent tube?

content.title: The Straight Tube vs Bent Tube Experiment
content.description: An animation showing a student looking through a straight pipe and successfully seeing a candle flame. Then, the pipe is bent, and the light rays from the candle hit the inside wall of the pipe and stop, showing that they cannot curve around the bend.

content: Just like a fast-moving train that cannot make a sharp turn without tracks, light cannot bend around corners. It always travels in straight lines. This property of light is known as **Rectilinear Propagation of Light**.

question: Why can't you see around a corner using just your eyes without a mirror?
options: Because your eyes are not powerful enough.
Because light loses its energy when it travels too far.
Because light travels only in straight lines and cannot bend around the corner.
Because the air pressure changes around the corner.

content: Try this! Take three square pieces of cardboard. Pierce a small hole in the exact center of each. Align them in a straight line and place a candle behind the last one. Look through the first hole. If you move the middle cardboard even slightly, the light disappears! This proves light only takes the straight path.

Think about ancient monuments like the Sun Temple in Konark, India. The architects knew about the straight-line travel of light and perfectly aligned the doors so that the first rays of the rising sun would travel in a perfectly straight path to illuminate the deity inside!

You can use this knowledge in real life! When a builder is aligning a wall, they often stretch a string perfectly tight. They know that a tight string forms a straight line, just like the path of light. This straight-line property is also why lasers are used in barcode scanners and targeting systems.

### The Mirror Mystery
Now, if light only travels in straight lines, how is it possible to see the back of your own head when you visit the barber? How does the light from the back of your head reach your eyes?

### What do you think?
Imagine throwing a bouncy rubber ball against a smooth, hard wall. What happens to the ball? Does it stick, pass through, or bounce back? What do you think light does when it hits a smooth, shiny surface like a mirror?

content.title: Bouncing Ball vs Bouncing Light
content.description: A split-screen animation. On the left, a rubber ball is thrown at an angle against a wall and bounces off at the same angle. On the right, a beam of light hits a flat mirror and bounces off perfectly at the same angle, demonstrating reflection.

content: When light hits a shiny, smooth surface, it bounces back, changing its direction. This is exactly like the rubber ball bouncing off a wall. This bouncing back of light is called the **Reflection of Light**.

question: What is the reflection of light?
options: Light passing through a clear glass.
Light bending when it enters water.
Light bouncing off a shiny surface like a mirror.
Light getting absorbed by a black shirt.

content: Reflection is the reason we can see anything that doesn't produce its own light. The moon doesn't glow; it just reflects the light from the sun. When you look in a mirror, the light from your face hits the mirror and bounces back into your eyes!

Many students think that all surfaces reflect light equally. That's not true! A rough surface scatters light in all directions, so you can't see your reflection in a wooden table. A smooth surface like a mirror reflects light in a perfect, orderly way, creating an image.

question: You are in a completely dark room with a mirror on the wall. If you shine a flashlight at the mirror, what will happen?
options: The mirror will absorb the light and stay dark.
The mirror will glow like a lamp.
The light will bounce off the mirror and light up another part of the room.
The light will pass right through the mirror.

content:
### The Rainbow Mystery
Have you ever wondered where the beautiful colors of a rainbow come from? After a rainy day, suddenly the sky paints a giant, colorful arch. But where do these colors hide when it's just a normal, sunny day?

### What do you think?
Sunlight looks completely 'white' to our eyes. But if sunlight is just white, how can it create seven vibrant colors in a rainbow? Is the water adding color to the light, or is the color already there?

content.title: The Prism and the Rainbow
content.description: A beam of white light enters a triangular glass prism. As it passes through, it magically splits apart, fanning out into the seven colors of the rainbow: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, and Violet.

content: It turns out, white light is actually a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow! When white light passes through water drops in the sky (or a glass prism), it gets split into its hidden colors. This splitting of white light into different colors is called **Dispersion of Light**.

question: What is actually happening when a rainbow is formed?
options: The sky is getting painted by the clouds.
The raindrops are adding colors to the sunlight.
The white sunlight is splitting into its hidden seven colors.
The sun changes its color after it rains.

content: Try it yourself: Get a CD or DVD and look at its shiny back under a light. You will see a mini rainbow! The tiny ridges on the CD split the white light just like raindrops do. You can also make a 'Newton's Disc' by painting the seven colors on a spinning top. When you spin it fast, the colors blend back together and look white!

In ancient India, the text 'Surya Siddhanta' accurately described the relationship between sunlight and colors. Sir Isaac Newton later famously proved with his prism experiment that white light is made of seven colors.

question: If you spin a disc painted with all seven colors of the rainbow very fast, what color will you see?
options: Black
White
Brown
A mix of all colors
